inlines.v: FEAT, noun [Latin factum, from facio, to perform.] 1. An act; a deed; an exploit; as a bold feat; a noble feat; feats of prowess. 2. In a subordinate sense, any extraordinary act of strength, skill or cunning, as feats of horsemanship, or of dexterity; a trick. FEAT, adjective Ready; skilful; ingenious. Never master had a page - so feat FEAT, verb transitive To form; to fashion.
